_purpose: Non-negotiable checks every future batch runs before reporting. Added after the paint-opacity defect reached four already-signed-off components.
1_instancePaintVerification: Place ONE INSTANCE of every new variant and read its RENDERED paints — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — comparing each against its master. Master-level reads are NOT evidence: paint-level opacity renders correctly on a master and incorrectly on an instance, which is exactly how the defect survived four batches. Any alpha must live in the variable's stored rgba, never as paint-level opacity. SCOPE: that last sentence governs UNBOUND paints only - for a BOUND paint Figma surfaces the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity, and that mirrored value is correct; read rule 9_boundPaintAlpha before touching it.
2_unboundPaintAudit: Walk EVERY top-level node on EVERY page, not just component sets. Reference frames, notes frames and loose glyphs count. Auditing only component sets is what let 3 unbound paints sit in the Radio reference frame across several batches.
3_referenceCounts: Count componentPropertyReferences per variant after any clone or combineAsVariants — cloning a variant inside a set silently drops them all.
4_skipInvisibleFalse: Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any audit walk, so boolean-hidden slots are inspected.
5_opacityLast: If paint-level opacity is genuinely unavoidable somewhere, apply it as the final operation AND verify on an instance. Prefer promoting to a computed variable.
6_enumerateDontRecall: When remediating or sweeping, enumerate from the file rather than from a previously reported list. The alpha remediation's known list was missing 18 of 48 paints.
7_fileIdentityFirst: Every Figma call passes fileKey YX2n4YLrEpBXNbcc73T6dw explicitly — never rely on an ambient or last-used file. Every session's FIRST Figma action verifies file identity against this schema's page inventory (figmaBuild.pages._order) before any read informs a decision or any write occurs; if the page list does not match, stop and report rather than proceeding. Added 2026-08-03 after a session read the legacy team library (ZPf0sJy83aPyrHjCVHomya, 'Tebra Working UI Kit') and produced a full reorganisation analysis against the wrong file. Note that figma.root.name returns 'Document' for both files, so the file NAME is not a usable identity check — the page list is.
8_roundWithRecord: Never carry a fractional dimension into Figma. Two cases, one treatment. (a) pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer exists behind the fraction: bind the intended integer, record computedPx. (b) Authored-fractional sources, where no intended integer exists — a fractional spacing multiplier, a viewBox ratio, a non-square viewBox in a square box: ROUND to the nearest integer and record the true value as computedPx in both the component description and the schema, and label the rounding a design decision with its source and date. Added 2026-08-03 when the primary nav produced the first case-(b) values (76.8, 44.8, 23.88, 18.24); Daniel ruled round-with-record as design authority. Intrinsic geometry is out of scope for this rule: VECTOR and GROUP bounds are the union of their path data, are not authored, and are not rounded — the tier 6 illustrations already set that precedent.
9_boundPaintAlpha: Before changing ANY paint-level opacity, first check whether that paint has a bound colour variable. If it does, Figma SURFACES the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity - it does NOT multiply the two. A paint bound to a variable storing rgba(0,0,0,0.87) correctly reads back paint.opacity 0.87 and renders at 0.87; that is the expected state, not a double-alpha defect, and it must be left alone. Forcing such a paint to opacity 1 DISCARDS the alpha and renders the node fully opaque. Rule 1's 'never as paint-level opacity' applies to UNBOUND paints only. Established empirically 2026-08-26 (checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry) after the opposite assumption produced a real regression on Alert filled/warning; reverted and audited library-wide 2026-08-27 (boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27). To re-confirm at any time: bind a rectangle to an alpha-carrying variable, never set opacity, then read paint.opacity back - it returns the variable's alpha.
10_cloneDropsPropertyRefs: Cloning a variant to add a new axis value DROPS componentPropertyReferences on every child. The clone keeps its layers and looks correct, but Label/icon-visibility/icon-swap stop responding — instance property values are stored yet never render, so a swapped instance silently shows the component default. After any variant clone, re-apply refs by copying them from a known-good sibling keyed on child layer name, then verify by reading a nested instance rendered characters against its property value, not just the property value. Hit during buttonInheritColour2026_08_28.
